shortDescription: The Baltic Exchange's dry bulk freight index fell on Friday and logged a weekly decline, as weaker capesize and panamax rates dragged the benchmark to its lowest level in more than a week.

children: The Baltic Exchange's dry bulk freight index fell on Friday and logged a weekly decline, as weaker capesize and panamax rates dragged the benchmark to its lowest level in more than a week.
, which tracks rates for capesize, panamax and supramax vessels, fell 14 points, or 0.4%, to 3,507, its lowest level since September 3. The index fell 3.3% for the week.
The capesize index (.BACI) was down 42 points, or 0.7%, at 6,080, posting a weekly loss of 5.3%.
Average daily earnings for capesize vessels (.BATCA), which typically transport 150,000-ton cargoes, including iron ore and coal, decreased by $380 to $51,636.

Iron ore prices fell for a third straight session and were heading for their first weekly loss in three, pressured by lower-than-anticipated demand and a sharp squeeze in steel margins in top consumer China.
The panamax index (.BPNI) fell 2 points, or 0.08%, to 2,407. The index was down 1.7% for the week.
Average daily earnings for panamax vessels (.BPWT), which usually carry 60,000 to 70,000 tons of coal or grain, fell $22 to $21,662.
The supramax index (.BSIS) was up 6 points, or 0.3%, at 1,719. The index gained 2.6% over the week.
